question.text: Ferdinand and his wife were assassinated by this 19-year old Yugoslav nationalist. He was a member of the Black Hand, which planned Franz Ferdinand's assassination.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.text: In this nation, the Gorbachev administration transferred power to Ion Iliescu [ill-YES-koo] after the revolt against, and public execution of, Nicolae Ceausescu [choh-SHESS-koo].
swap.clue: One dictator in this country lost support for his rule after he ordered protestors supporting Laszlo Tokes in Timisoara to be fired upon.

question.text: This former president of Yugoslavia was put on trial for crimes against humanity, but he died during the proceedings at the Hague. He allegedly committed genocide in Kosovo.
question.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

swap.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
swap.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
swap.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

question.leadin: This politician was overthrown in a revolt that began at Timisoara.
question.text: Name this communist politician who succeeded Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej and built the Centrul Civic.
question.clue: This man, who used the Securitate secret police, was the only leader subjected to a violent overthrow during the anti-Communist Revolutions of 1989.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Soviet bloc countries.
swap.text: This country was led by Enver Hoxha, and they were pretty close friends with China.
swap.clue: This nation was flooded with refugees from the nearby Kosovo War, and joined NATO in 2009.

question.text: This 1884 conference organized by the German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck regulated the rules of colonization and attempted to eliminate African autonomy and self-independence.
question.clue: Another key participant here was Gyula Andrassy, who negotiated the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by Austria-Hungary.

swap.text: This archbishop, recognized as the Father of Greek Cyprus, was overthrown in the 1974 coup but returned soon after as the Greek junta collapsed later that year. He served as the country's first president from 1960 to 1977.
swap.clue: The junta collapsed after their sponsorship of a coup deposing this ethnarch of Cyprus ended in a Turkish counter-invasion known as Operation Atilla.

question.leadin: Name these East European Communist leaders.
question.text: He seized Albania in 1944 and ruled until succeeded by Ramiz Alia in 1981.
question.clue: A vocal opponent of Mao (+) Zedong's "three worlds" theory, this man was abandoned by his closest ally, China, and successfully imposed state atheism despite his country's majority Muslim population.

swap.text: Former capitals of this region include Campulung and Curtea de Arges. Distinct from the mountainous Transylvania, for 15 points, name this region that contains Bucharest, and that united with Moldavia to form Romania.
swap.clue: This region was the first one to be ruled by Michael the Brave.

question.leadin: Though famous for other reasons, this man was known as a playwright and novelist throughout his life, authoring such works as The Truth that Killed.
question.text: Name this dissident who was assassinated in London in 1978. The murder has been traced to a secret service agent codenamed "Piccadilly", whose real identity is often suspected to be the Danish citizen Francesco Gullino.
question.clue: This Bulgarian dissident who was infamously assassinated in 1978 when a pellet containing ricin was fired from an umbrella into his leg.

swap.text: The Hungarian Revolution was partially put down by Josip Jelacic ("YO-seep YAY-la-cheech"), a military leader of this ethnicity. Nationalists of this ethnicity formed the Ustase ("OO-stah-sheh") during World War II.
swap.clue: People of this nationality received very little power over taxation in a dissatisfying agreement called the Nagodba, which did, however, allow them to elect their sabor.

question.text: Benedetto Cotrugli, an economist from this city, described an early version of double-entry bookkeeping. This city became a major maritime republic after being transferred from Venice to Hungary in the Treaty of Zadar.
question.clue: The nobles of this city elected its leaders to a position known as either Rector or knez ("k'nez").

swap.leadin: During the Log Revolution, people native to one of these two modern-day countries constructed blockades made of logs in the other, rejecting changes made after a 1990 election.
swap.text: Name these two former members of Yugoslavia. Paramilitary units from one of them perpetrated the Vukovar Massacre in the other.
swap.answerHtml: Serbia and Croatia [or Republic of Serbia and Republic of Croatia; accept Republika Hrvatska in place of “Croatia”; accept Republika Srbija in place of “Serbia”; do not accept answers mentioning “Republika Srpska,” because that’s different]

question.text: This man joined with the Iron Guard to establish the National Legionary State in 1940, but was overthrown by the return of King Michael for his Nazi collaboration.
question.clue: This leader's army launched Operation Munchen to reclaim Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina, and massacred Jews in Odessa and Iasi.

swap.text: As the Red Army marched into Romania, this King launched a coup against Antonescu and joined the Allies. The Soviet post-war occupation forced his abdication and exile until the overthrow of Nicolae Ceausescu.

question.leadin: The organization headed by this man carried out a reign of terror in the 1930s that included the Velebit Uprising and it responded to King Alexander I's challenge to kill him by doing just that.
question.text: Name this leader of the Ustase movement, who used that position to persecute Jews, Serbs and Roma in concentration camps like Jasenovac.

swap.text: This failed 1944 action directed by Skorzeny was an attempt to kill Tito and end the resistance in Yugoslavia; partisan agents discovered the plot ahead of time and thwarted it.

question.text: NATO attacked Yugoslavia after the failure of this 1999 treaty, which granted temporary autonomy to Kosovo.

swap.leadin: This man fled to German after a Nazi-backed rebellion by the organization he led turned unsuccessful.
swap.text: Identify this man, who held the post of Deputy Prime Minister during Ion Antonescu's reign.
